A patient has recurrent urinary tract infections. What exams should be considered?

Note: the following critical exams are still pending and should be prioritized: urine culture.
resposta:
Recurrent UTI in diabetic patients is most commonly due to Diabetes mellitus which leads to rise blood glucose levels that causes osmotic diuresis resulting dilutional nephropathy giving susceptibility of infection.It also may occur because diabetes can cause damage to nerves leading loss reflexes and inability to void promptly enough , allowing bacteria to multiply.Therefore you must get your sugar under control, do daily check up with urinalysis.Urine test will help us identify type organisms causing this problem.Antibiotic cover as per sensitivity report will treat it completely.Ensure adequate hydration.
